translationRepairs: He, Cui Yanjin, Li Hanqiong, and Liu Yu split the siege: Han took the northeast, Liu Yu the northwest facing Liu Jiyuan's strongest walls. Yu wanted to trade sectors; Han said, "Your commission outranks mine in title but not in peril—the northeast is where you belong."

He, Cui Yanjin, Li Hanqiong, and Liu Yu split the siege: Han took the northeast, Liu Yu the northwest facing Liu Jiyuan's strongest walls. Yu wanted to trade sectors; Han said, "A surveillance commissioner ranks lower, so I should take the northeast."
觀察使班次下，當部東北 means Cao Han, a mere surveillance commissioner of lower rank, says he should keep the northeast; the current English invents a different meaning.
He was soon made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and charged with frontier defense and river-control works.
He was soon made Recipient of Edicts in the Bureau of Military Affairs and charged with guarding the breached river dikes.
樞密承旨 is a Recipient of Edicts, not a commissioner; 護塞決河 means supervising the closing of the river breach.
His sons Chongyi served as spare-stable commissioner and Chonggui as a gate attendant.
His sons: Chongyi served as commissioner of the spare stables, and Chonggui as an audience usher.
Grammatical repair; 閤門祗候 is an audience usher, not a gate attendant.
When Khitan raiders in the tens of thousands struck Zhongshan, he routed them at Mancheng, pursued to Suicheng, and took ten thousand heads and captives, receiving the honorary title Grand Guardian.

When Khitan raiders in the tens of thousands struck Zhongshan, he routed them at Mancheng, pursued to Suicheng, and took ten thousand heads and captives, receiving the honorary title Acting Grand Commandant.
檢校太尉 is Acting (honorary) Grand Commandant, not Grand Guardian.
At his accession Xin became commander of the Palace Front and chief attendant.
At Taizu's accession Xin became commander of the Palace Front and was promoted to chief attendant.
The accession is Taizu's, not Xin's.
In autumn of Taiping Xingguo 2, martial exercises were held in the western suburbs. Palace Front commander Yang Xin was stricken mute, and Han was ordered to stand in for him.
In autumn of Taiping Xingguo 2, martial exercises were held in the western suburbs. Palace Front commander Yang Xin had fallen ill and lost his voice, and Han was ordered to stand in for him.
病瘖 means fell ill and became mute.

unresolvedReferences.description: Li Hanqiong's great-grandfather Yu has no dated activity in the chapter; intervening grandfather and father are unnamed.
Xin's surname (Mi 米) appears only in the biography heading s0189, outside this packet.
The 四年 of Xin's recall follows Duangong 2 (which had only two years); the era is not restated, so the year is bounded to Chunhua (990–994) rather than fixed.
The 二年 transfer to Zhen'an follows Yongxi 4 without restating the era; bounded to 988–989 (likely Duangong 2).
